title: HATT: Hamiltonian Adaptive Ternary Tree for Optimizing Fermion-to-Qubit Mapping
problem: Mapping Fermionic quantum systems to qubit systems produces Hamiltonians with high Pauli weight, inflating quantum circuit gate count and depth. Existing Fermion-to-qubit mappings are not tailored to specific Hamiltonian structures, leading to unnecessary overhead.
method: HATT constructs ternary tree-based Fermion-to-qubit mappings using a bottom-up procedure that is adaptive to the specific Fermionic Hamiltonian being compiled. The algorithm analyzes Hamiltonian term structure to guide tree construction, reducing Pauli weight compared to generic mappings such as Jordan-Wigner or Bravyi-Kitaev. The complexity is reduced from O(N^4) to O(N^3) while preserving vacuum state properties required for correctness of simulation.

title: MemSeer: Leverage Memory Failure Distinctions and Multi-Grained Prediction in Ultra-Scale Heterogeneous X86/ARM Clusters
problem: In ultra-scale heterogeneous cloud clusters mixing x86 and ARM platforms, DRAM failures are a primary cause of server downtime; existing prediction methods fail to account for architecture-specific failure patterns and require single-scale predictions.
method: MemSeer analyzes memory failure characteristics across x86/ARM platforms and employs multi-grained prediction (multiple timescale levels) integrated into AIOps to predict failures. Achieves 17.3% F1-score improvement and 27% recall improvement.

title: SDM-PEB: Spatial-Depthwise Mamba for Enhanced Post-Exposure Bake Simulation
problem: Post-exposure bake (PEB) simulation requires precise 3D modeling of photoacid diffusion and inhibitor reactions to ensure resist profile accuracy and circuit pattern fidelity in semiconductor lithography.
method: SDM-PEB uses a hierarchical feature extractor with overlapped patch merging and efficient self-attention, combined with a spatial-depthwise Mamba-based attention unit employing customized selective scan and structured state space models to capture both coarse and fine features at multiple scales and 3D dependencies.

title: Symmetry-Based Synthesis for Interpretable Boolean Evaluation
problem: Boolean function synthesis for >6 inputs intractable; state-of-the-art requires hyper-parameter tuning; poor interpretability
method: Symmetry-based remapping engine inspired by Edward's theory; synthesize functions up to 20 inputs via recursive substructure discovery

title: MambaOPU: An FPGA Overlay Processor for State-space-duality-based Mamba Models
problem: Mamba2 state-space models are memory-bound due to irregular broadcast element-wise multiplications and structured sparse computations; neither CPU nor standard GPU achieve good compute efficiency.
method: FPGA overlay processor using: (1) operator fusion combining broadcast multiply and summation into single descriptor, backward shifting embeds segment multiply in subsequent ops to reduce path length; (2) sparse computation skipping via tensor-reorder-and-group + sparse data fetcher; (3) reconfigurable systolic array for linear operation support with improved data reuse.

title: An Efficient Bit-level Sparse MAC-accelerated Architecture with SW/HW Co-design on FPGA
problem: Bit-level sparsity exploitation for MAC units is a proven efficiency improvement, but FPGA implementations face architectural limitations; existing FPGA designs lack effective bit-level sparsity support compared to ASIC value-aware accelerators.
method: Software/hardware co-design solution introducing LUT-friendly encoding with adaptable granularity that maps efficiently to FPGA LUTs, combined with hardware supporting multiplication time uncertainty to handle variable-latency sparse operations. This approach balances redundancy elimination with accuracy preservation and FPGA compatibility.

title: SplitSync: Bank Group-Level Split-Synchronization for High-Performance DRAM PIM
problem: DRAM PIM architectures with bank-level SIMD parallelism suffer from synchronous execution requiring all banks to activate before computation. Row activation overhead exceeds computation time, limiting performance. Asynchronous approaches reduce overhead but require large shared accumulators per bank, increasing area.
method: Bank group (BG) level split-synchronization: each BG operates asynchronously to hide row activation overhead while operating synchronously within a BG to eliminate shared accumulators. Hybrid approach balances activation hide and area efficiency.

title: A Single-Link Multi-Domain-Output (SLiMDO) Isolated DC-DC Converter with Passive Magnetic Flux Sharing for Local Energy Distribution and Rx Behavior Sensing-Based Global Power Modulation
problem: Galvanically isolated DC-DC converters with multiple domain-specific outputs require separate control signals across isolation barriers and custom interconnect topologies, increasing complexity and requiring digital isolators for Tx-Rx communication.
method: Single-link topology using passive magnetic flux sharing and receiver-side behavior sensing for global power modulation, eliminating need for digital isolators and enabling flexible domain-specific output configuration.

title: ESM: A Framework for Building Effective Surrogate Models for Hardware-Aware Neural Architecture Search
problem: Hardware-aware NAS relies on surrogate models to efficiently predict performance (latency, energy) of DNN candidates on target devices, but building accurate, reliable prediction models requires systematic understanding of factors influencing prediction quality.
method: Systematic analysis of surrogate model types and their strengths/weaknesses for GPU-powered devices. Studies factors influencing prediction accuracy across all pipeline stages (data generation, model selection, training). Presents ESM framework enabling reliable dataset generation and efficient model generation with cost-aware optimization.

title: LA-MTL: Latency-Aware Automated Multi-Task Learning
problem: Multi-task learning on embedded devices must simultaneously optimize task accuracy, parameter efficiency, and inference latency, but existing MTL approaches lack explicit latency constraints in the search, often requiring post-hoc tuning that compromises accuracy or efficiency.
method: LA-MTL performs layer-level automated MTL policy search incorporating a novel Analytical Latency Factor (ALF) that captures local and global latencies during search. The framework derives Pareto-optimal solutions balancing task metrics, parameter efficiency, and latency constraints via architecture search on shared backbone layers.

title: Supporting Register-based Addressing Modes for in-DRAM PIM ISAs
problem: In-DRAM Processing-in-Memory architectures incur two critical overheads: PIM code offloading to memory and data transfers between CPU and memory, limiting speedup potential for DNN inference despite eliminating compute-memory bottleneck.
method: Two register-based addressing modes—indexed and base-offset—are added to DMA descriptor-based in-DRAM PIM ISAs. These modes reduce CPU-memory transfer overhead and PIM code offloading cost by enabling efficient descriptor composition and reducing descriptor complexity.

title: Palermo: Improving the Performance of Oblivious Memory using Protocol-Hardware Co-Design
problem: Oblivious RAM (ORAM) protocols impose severe performance penalties because classical ORAM enforces strict sequential dependencies between memory operations, leaving memory bandwidth severely underutilized. Prior prefetching and request-elimination approaches are fragile under low-locality workloads and create additional ORAM stash pressure overhead.
method: Palermo redesigns the RingORAM protocol to allow overlapping of memory operations both within a single ORAM request and across multiple concurrent requests, without violating correctness or security invariants. A dedicated ORAM controller hardware implements this relaxed protocol by concurrently issuing memory requests while tracking and enforcing only the necessary inter-request dependencies to maintain a consistent ORAM tree view. The architecture manages stash and position-map structures in hardware to prevent stash overflow while enabling pipelined DRAM accesses.

title: Cooperative Graceful Degradation in Containerized Clouds
problem: Cloud operators lack a mechanism to automatically perform graceful degradation of applications during failures or capacity crunch while simultaneously satisfying application availability requirements and operator infrastructure objectives.
method: Phoenix uses criticality tags on containers to distinguish critical from non-critical services, then applies diagonal scaling—turning off non-critical containers during capacity crunch to free resources for critical services. A Kubernetes-atop controller implements this cooperative graceful degradation by jointly optimizing for both application-defined criticality constraints and operator-level infrastructure objectives. Phoenix handles failures in a cluster of 100,000 nodes within 10 seconds.

title: Reinforcement Learning-Guided Graph State Generation in Photonic Quantum Computers
problem: In photonic quantum computers (PQCs), generating graph states (entangled photon collections) requires finding an optimal generation sequence over quantum emitters, where three fidelity-critical metrics — generation time, number of emitters used, and number of CZ gates — are jointly minimized. Existing compilation frameworks either face exponential search complexity or fail to guarantee optimal results due to their non-deterministic properties.
method: RLGS (Reinforcement Learning-guided Graph State generation) frames the generation sequence problem as an RL optimization task. A map-based abstraction extracts and aligns two-qubit gate dependencies from quantum circuits into a structured representation, enabling the RL agent to detect dependency patterns and search for generation sequences that simultaneously reduce generation time, emitter count, and CZ gate insertions. The framework balances gate serialization depth against crosstalk reduction.

title: From Optimal to Practical: Efficient Micro-op Cache Replacement Policies for Data Center Applications
problem: Data center applications suffer frequent micro-op (uop) cache misses because no effective uop-cache-specific replacement policy exists; the uop cache has fundamentally different cost characteristics from conventional caches (variable and disproportional miss costs, partial hits), making standard policies like LRU and even Belady's algorithm suboptimal.
method: FLACK is introduced as a near-optimal offline replacement policy that accounts for uop cache-specific properties: variable miss costs (due to disproportional re-fetch penalties) and partial hits (when only some micro-ops of an instruction group are cached). FLACK substantially outperforms Belady's algorithm, establishing a new uop-cache-specific optimality bound. FURBYS is then designed as a practical online policy that mimics FLACK via profile-guided methods, using three components: (1) whole-execution hit/miss profiles per static instruction, (2) detection of locally/transiently hot data, and (3) selective ignorance of entries with profiled low hit rates during replacement decisions.

title: A Novel Covert Timing Channel for Cloud FPGAs
problem: Cloud FPGA users face covert data exfiltration risk via side-channel attacks that minimize detection by both victims and cloud providers.
method: Exploits AXI protocol handshake signals and Internet interpacket delay to establish covert timing channel from cloud FPGA to external attacker. Uses timing modulation of AXI handshakes (backpressure, valid/ready) to encode exfiltrated data into network packet timing. Minimal traffic signature avoids cloud provider detection.
